blocks.text: *How you grow — the six base stats, and the Ring that scales your power.*
Primary stats
Six base stats you allocate as you level — **anyone can raise any of them** (there are no classes):

items: **STR** — melee attack power and how much you can carry
**DEX** — ranged attack power, accuracy and cast speed

blocks.text: **You choose your starting stats when you create a character**, by pulling the corners of a hexagon. Opposite stats — STR and INT, AGI and LUK, VIT and DEX — always add up to 10, so raising one lowers its partner, and every shape spends all your starting points. After that you get points to spend as you level, and **each point into a stat costs more the higher that stat already is** — every block of ten gets pricier. So a lopsided build is genuinely expensive: going all-in on one stat buys fewer total points than spreading out. What you can afford is fixed by your level; nothing else grants stat points.
What each point actually buys

Every stat feeds several numbers at once — that spread is what makes a build. On top of that, **every time a stat reaches a multiple of 10 — gear included — it jumps one number up**: +4 at 10, +6 at 20, +22 at 100, each jump bigger than the last. The exact per-point values:

rows: +1 MELEE ATK and +½ RANGED ATK, and +30 to how much you can carry. STR's jump goes to MELEE ATK.
+1 FLEE (dodge), and +0.5% attack speed. AGI's jump goes to FLEE.
+2% max HP, +⅓ DEF, and health regeneration worth 0.02% of your max HP every second. VIT's jump goes to DEF.
+1 M.ATK, +1.5% max MP, +⅓ M.DEF, mana regeneration worth 0.02% of your max MP every second, and steadier magic damage. INT's jump goes to M.ATK.
+1 RANGED ATK, +1 HIT (accuracy), +½ MELEE ATK, +0.125% attack speed, steadier physical damage, and a shorter cast wind-up — reaching **instant casting at 150 DEX**. DEX's jump goes to RANGED ATK.

+0.3% crit chance, +0.2% crit damage, +¼ MELEE ATK, +¼ RANGED ATK, +¼ M.ATK, +⅓ HIT, +⅕ FLEE — and it works defensively too: your LUK lowers an attacker's crit chance against you by 0.3% per point. LUK's jump goes to crit damage, counted in percent.

blocks.text: **Nothing in combat can change these six.** No buff, debuff, potion or ailment touches a primary stat — they come from your points and your gear alone. What skills move instead is the list below.
Every number on your sheet, and what feeds it
These are the numbers combat actually reads. A buff or debuff can move any of them for a while; your primaries and your gear set where they sit at rest.

blocks.text: Numbers your stats don't touch
A few things come from somewhere other than your six stats. They're real numbers that matter in a fight — they just aren't bought with points.

rows: your character's own speed, multiplied by whatever is slowing or hastening you
none from gear — only the Fist's defence skills block *(coming with its skills)*
none from gear — a skill can add jumps to your thrown shuriken and your bouncing skills for a while *(coming with its skills)*
Neutral, unless an Armor Converter is running — then its element, at level 1. Incoming attacks are scaled against it
a flat pool of 100. Sprinting drains 25 a second; it refills at 30 standing still, 18 walking, and 8 doing anything else
0 at rest — they exist only while a card or a skill grants them
a percentage taken off a hit *before* DEF subtracts its flat amount. Monsters can be built with it; you have none yet

blocks.text: How regeneration works

HP and MP both tick back up on their own, several times a second, and the fraction is never lost — a rate too small to pay a whole point this tick is carried to the next, so 0.3 a second really is 0.3 a second.
A debuff can **stop** your regeneration but can never reverse it. Push a regen rate below zero and it simply pays nothing — it will not drain you, and it will not heal an enemy you cast it on.

Any time your HP goes up — a potion, a heal, natural regeneration, anything added later — you'll see the same **green number** float over your head. Monsters get it too, so you can always see when something is healing itself.
The Ring — your growth engine

The Ring is a **closed loop of ten percentage-based passive stats** that you build up as you level. It is part of your character — nothing to wear, nothing to lose — and a separate layer from your weapons: **a weapon's mastery points buy your skills**, and the **Ring scales their power**. Your progress on the Ring is saved with your character.
The ten Ring stats
Going clockwise around the loop:
**Defense → HP → Attack → Accuracy → Cast Speed → Magic Attack → MP → Evasion → Critical → Attack Speed →** *(back to Defense)*

The two **poles sit dead-opposite: Defense (top) and Magic Attack (bottom)**, with the survival stats bridging them — so drifting from a physical toward a magic build naturally carries you across the defenses in between.
Two stats do double duty: **Defense** raises both your physical *and* magic defense (there is no separate magic-defense stat), and **Critical** raises both your crit rate *and* your crit damage.
The draft — a steering wheel
Every level-up you pick **one of four** options:

items: **Three known** — your current stat plus its **two neighbors** on the ring (a sliding window of three).
**One wildcard** — a random stat from elsewhere on the ring.

blocks.text: Picking the center keeps stacking that stat; picking a neighbor slides your window that way; the wildcard jumps you across the ring.
Percentage growth with a soft cap

Ring stats give **percentage multipliers**, not flat points, so they never go obsolete as your gear grows. Growth follows a **soft cap**: most stats climb toward a **+80% ceiling**, while **Critical caps at +50%** and **Evasion at +60%** (both would break combat if left uncapped). Because each extra rank is worth a little less, the math **rewards spreading out** — though single-stacking is always allowed.
Your Ring locks your role

**Most of a skill's power is your Ring** — and that scaling is role-bound: **healing scales off MP**, **damage scales off Attack / Magic Attack**. So a support who invested MP hits like wet paper with a damage weapon, and a damage build heals for crumbs with a staff. A skill's own level adds to that (see *Skills*), but the weight of it stays bound to the stats you chose. **Changing weapons changes which skills you may use — never the stats behind them.**
*(Ring upgrades that add whole new behaviors from investment are a planned future addition — for now the Ring only scales numbers.)*
Monsters use this exact system

Everything on this page describes **monsters too**. They have the same six stats, the same formulas behind them, the same rising cost per point, and the same level-based budget — a level 20 monster carries what a level 20 player could have bought. They wear real equipment, and a monster can carry Ring investment of its own that scales it on this same soft-cap curve.
There is no difficulty multiplier anywhere. A monster is hard because of its level, its stats, and its gear — the same three things that make you hard. See *Monsters*.
Reading your character sheet
Press **C** to open your character sheet. It lists every number that decides how you fight, and it updates **live** — buffs and debuffs appear the moment they land and vanish when they run out.
The big number is always **your own stat**. Anything a buff or debuff is doing to it sits in **parentheses** right after it:

items: **Green** — something is helping you, e.g. `MELEE ATK 120-140 (+24)`
**Red** — something is hurting you, e.g. `HIT 82 (-30)` while blinded
**No parentheses** — nothing is affecting that stat right now

blocks.text: The sheet reads from the same numbers combat does, so what you see is exactly what you hit for — never an estimate.
What you'll find on it:

rows: MELEE ATK · RANGED ATK · M.ATK · CRIT chance and crit damage · HIT
DEF and M.DEF (plus their flat damage cut) · FLEE · GUARD · BARRIER
ASPD (attack speed) · CAST (between casts) · WIND-UP (cast time) · MOVE and RUN speed
LEECH (HP from damage) · MP LEECH · REFLECT
